rows.text: Who are the authors of 'Attention Is All You Need' and what year was it published?
rows.label: paper_lookup
rows.rationale: Asks for the author list and year of one paper named by exact title (arXiv 1706.03762); these are metadata facts, not a formatted reference (citation) and not an explanation of attention (concept).

rows.text: What are the key papers on parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large language models?
rows.label: literature_search
rows.rationale: Asks to find a set of papers on a topic rather than facts about one named paper, so literature_search rather than paper_lookup; no explanation of the method itself is requested, so not concept.

rows.text: Give me the BibTeX entry for 'Attention Is All You Need'.
rows.label: citation
rows.rationale: The requested output is a formatted reference; the paper is named only so the BibTeX can be built, which separates this from paper_lookup where the student wants facts about the paper.

rows.text: What is attention in neural networks, and why does it help with long sequences?
rows.label: concept
rows.rationale: Tricky: asks for an explanation of a method with no paper named or identified by id. The nearest paper ('Attention Is All You Need') is never mentioned, so paper_lookup does not apply.

rows.text: Can you pull up the abstract for arXiv 2106.09685? I want to know what it claims before reading the whole thing.
rows.label: paper_lookup
rows.rationale: One paper identified by arXiv id (LoRA), and the abstract is one of the listed facts; there is no topic to search (not literature_search) and no reference format requested (not citation).

rows.text: Hi! Are you able to help me with my research today?
rows.label: other
rows.rationale: A greeting with no paper, topic, reference, or method asked about; none of the four research intents fits, and the nearest one (literature_search) would need an actual topic.

rows.text: Can you find me papers on LLM agents that use external tools or APIs? I'm starting a literature review for my thesis.
rows.label: literature_search
rows.rationale: Topic-level request to find several papers (ReAct, Toolformer, Reflexion would match); no single paper is named, so not paper_lookup, and no reference format is requested, so not citation.

rows.text: I need to cite the ReAct paper (arXiv 2210.03629) in APA format for my thesis.
rows.label: citation
rows.rationale: Tricky: names one paper by arXiv id, which looks like paper_lookup, but the deliverable is an APA-formatted reference, so the intent is citation.

rows.text: Can you explain how the reparameterization trick works in variational autoencoders?
rows.label: concept
rows.rationale: Asks how a technique works without naming or identifying a paper; 'Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes' is in the data but the student is not asking about that paper, so not paper_lookup.

rows.text: What venue did 'Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition' appear in, and in what year?
rows.label: paper_lookup
rows.rationale: Venue and year of a single paper named by exact title (arXiv 1512.03385) are listed metadata facts; the student wants the facts themselves, not a formatted reference, so not citation.

rows.text: I've read 'Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models'. Which later papers build on or extend that idea?
rows.label: literature_search
rows.rationale: Tricky: a paper is named by exact title, but the question is about other papers related to it, i.e. finding a set of works (Tree of Thoughts, ReAct, Reflexion), so literature_search rather than paper_lookup.

rows.text: A reference in my draft reads: Devlin, J., Chang, M.-W., Lee, K., & Toutanova, K. (2019). BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding. arXiv:1810.04805. Is this a real paper and is the citation correct?
rows.label: citation
rows.rationale: Tricky: the student is checking whether an existing reference is real and correctly formatted, which is the verification half of citation; they are not asking for new facts about the paper, so not paper_lookup.

rows.text: What's the difference between fine-tuning a model and in-context learning?
rows.label: concept
rows.rationale: Compares two general ideas without naming any paper; 'Language Models are Few-Shot Learners' is the natural source but is not referenced, so not paper_lookup.

rows.text: Is arXiv 2302.13971 the Llama 2 paper or the original LLaMA paper? I have the two ids mixed up in my notes.
rows.label: paper_lookup
rows.rationale: Tricky: asks which title belongs to one specific arXiv id (it is 'LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models'; Llama 2 is 2307.09288), a metadata fact about one paper. The student is not asking for a formatted reference or checking a bibliography entry, so not citation.

rows.text: List the most cited papers on applying transformers to image classification, ranked by citation count.
rows.label: literature_search
rows.rationale: Find-and-rank request over a topic using Semantic Scholar citation counts; no single paper is named, so not paper_lookup, and 'citation count' does not make it a citation request since no reference is to be produced or verified.

rows.text: My .bib entry for the Vision Transformer paper (arXiv 2010.11929) lists only Dosovitskiy as the author and has no year field. Can you check it against the real paper and give me a corrected BibTeX entry?
rows.label: citation
rows.rationale: Tricky: names one paper by arXiv id and mentions authors and year, which looks like paper_lookup, but the student is correcting an existing reference and wants a BibTeX entry back, so the task is citation.

rows.text: How does RLHF work at a high level? I don't understand the reward model part.
rows.label: concept
rows.rationale: Asks for an explanation of a training method without naming a paper; 'Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback' is the obvious paper but is not mentioned, so not paper_lookup.

rows.text: Who wrote the Sentence-BERT paper, and when did it come out?
rows.label: paper_lookup
rows.rationale: Authors and date of one paper identified by its well-known short title (arXiv 1908.10084); the student wants the facts, not a formatted reference, so not citation.

rows.text: Are there any pre-2016 papers on deep generative models I should read for background, like the GAN or VAE papers?
rows.label: literature_search
rows.rationale: Asks for a set of papers on a topic with a date filter; GAN and VAE are examples of the topic, not a single paper the student wants facts about, so not paper_lookup.

rows.text: Can you proofread the introduction paragraph of my thesis for grammar and flow?
rows.label: other
rows.rationale: An editing request about the student's own writing; it names no paper, search topic, reference, or method, so none of the four research intents applies, even though the context is academic.
